r0.why: Before the Phanerozoic [1]; named after preceding the Cambrian, Cambria/Wales [2]; 88% [3]; three eons [4]; 4.6 Ga to 538.8 Ma, hard-shelled creatures [5].

r1.why: General use without eon name [12]; USGS and ICS regard it as informal [13]; supereon informal, not defined by ICS [14].

r2.why: Eight-ninths, little known, mostly since 1960s [6]; poorer fossil record, stromatolites of limited use [7]; metamorphism, erosion, burial [8].

r3.why: Coalesced ~4,543 Ma [9]; Theia and Moon [10]; stable crust by 4,433 Ma, zircons 4,404 +/- 8 Ma [11].

r4.why: No date for origin of life [17]; Greenland carbon [18]; 3.46 Gyr bacteria fossils [19]; >4.280 Gyr evidence [21]; 2100 Ma multicellular [23]; Ediacaran soft-bodied forms worldwide [24],[25].

r5.why: Oxygen only after photosynthesis [41]; combined with iron then accumulated [43],[44]; banded iron formations [45]; glacial periods [39]; Sturtian-Varangian Snowball Earth [40].

r6.why: Tectonics hard to interpret [36]; proto-continents before 4280 Ma, supercontinent ~1130 Ma [37]; Rodinia broke up ~750 Ma [38].
